findings: The current overall-award COVID/IIJA exclusion is not a stable default transaction filter across years; removed amounts range from $706,010,366.00 to $46,809,055,161.81.
Broad non-Q DEFC exclusion continues to over-exclude mixed award-history transactions; removed amounts range from $0.00 to $46,937,047,042.81.

The profile-aligned exclusion is more conservative than broad DEFC, but it does not land close to Funding Profiles non-VFC/non-emergency targets in FY2020-FY2023; removed amounts range from $56,480,905.00 to $14,165,096,328.00.

FY2023 is consistent with FY2020-FY2022 on closest-scenario behavior: all available Funding Profiles years are closest to the current overall-award COVID/IIJA exclusion, and FY2023's residual difference falls within the FY2020-FY2022 range.

FY2021 is the strangest year: no-exclusion and profile-aligned totals are much higher than the Funding Profiles non-VFC/non-emergency target because a very large share of obligations sits on awards with supplemental/DEFC history.
Keep VFC exclusion separate from emergency/supplemental exclusion.
recommendations.recommended_next_methodology_update: Add supplemental-history and profile-aligned exclusion fields first, keep the map default mixed-award tolerant, and expose Funding Profiles comparison mode as a separate diagnostic/calibration view before changing public map defaults.
